info.title: Skill Trees API
info.description: Backend API for a public skill-tree sharing site. Reading is public and needs no account; creating or changing a tree requires a session, and a tree may only be modified by the account that created it. Zero external dependencies: node:http and node:sqlite only. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) that keep the older `error` (and, for rejected imports, `problems`) members. Every GET also answers HEAD. A known path asked with a method it doesn't take answers 405 with an Allow header (components/responses/MethodNotAllowed), and OPTIONS answers Allow with no CORS headers: cross-origin use is unsupported. A request body must be declared application/json, or it is refused with 415. Cross-site requests are refused with 403 unless they are top-level GET navigations (W3C Fetch Metadata), as are state-changing requests whose Origin is another host. Responses are compressed (br, gzip) when the client accepts it, and GETs carry an ETag and answer If-None-Match with 304.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Accounts, sessions, and sign-in through GitHub, Google or an OpenID Connect provider

tags.name: Passkeys
tags.description: Sign-up, sign-in and management with passkeys (W3C Web Authentication Level 3). Only when PUBLIC_ORIGIN is set; otherwise every route but config answers 404.

201.description: Account created; a session cookie is set

200.description: Signed in; a session cookie is set

post.summary: Sign out and invalidate the session
post.description: Deletes the session server-side and clears the cookie. Also sends Clear-Site-Data: "cookies", so the browser drops every cookie this site set — a leftover plain-named session cookie from before the __Host- rename, and the flow cookie of an unfinished provider sign-in.

200.description: Signed out; the session cookie is cleared
The current account, or null when signed out

get.summary: The providers "Continue with ..." is offered for
get.description: Every provider configured on this server (GitHub, Google, a generic OpenID Connect provider). Empty when none is. Only an id and a label: never a client id or secret.

200.description: Configured providers, possibly none

post.summary: Begin signing in (or connecting an account) through a provider
post.description: Creates a single-use, ten-minute flow server-side (state, PKCE S256 verifier, OIDC nonce, the validated next path) and returns the provider's authorization URL, which the page then navigates to. Sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie binding the flow to this browser (__Host-skilltree_oauth over HTTPS, skilltree_oauth otherwise). A POST with a JSON body rather than a link or form so the same-origin check guards it (a GET start with intent=link would be CSRF-able) and so CSP form-action 'self' never meets a redirect off-site. intent=link requires a session and attaches the provider account to it. Throttled per address; a completed sign-in gives its count back.

200.description: Where to send the browser; the flow cookie is set

403.description: The request came from another site (Origin does not match)

503.description: The provider could not be reached (discovery failed), or too many sign-ins are unfinished

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back (the redirect_uri)
get.description: Not called by the page: the provider redirects here. The flow is looked up by state and deleted in the same step (single use), must carry this browser's flow cookie (login CSRF), must belong to this provider (mix-up), and must bring back iss equal to the provider's issuer when present — required when the provider advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported (RFC 9207). The code is exchanged with the PKCE verifier and the same redirect_uri; an ID token is verified (signature against the JWKS, iss, aud/azp, exp/iat/nbf, nonce) or, for GitHub, the numeric user id is read from /user. Signs in to the account holding that (issuer, subject) — or a new one; never matched by email — or, for intent=link, connects it to the signed-in account. Always answers 303 and always clears the flow cookie.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the provider when it did not issue a code; access_denied means the person declined.

303.description: Signed in or connected: to the flow's next path, with a fresh session cookie when signing in. Refused: to /account.html?oauth_error=<code>, where code is one of cancelled, expired, failed, unavailable, identity_taken, link_session — never text from the provider — plus &next= for a sign-in whose flow was found.

get.summary: The provider accounts connected to the signed-in account

200.description: Connected provider accounts, oldest first

delete.description: Refused with 409 when it is the last way to sign in: an account keeps at least one of a password, a passkey for the current RP ID, or a connected provider that is configured now. Another account's identity answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

200.description: Disconnected

409.description: It is the only remaining way to sign in

get.summary: Whether passkeys are on, and for which RP ID
get.description: Passkeys are on only when PUBLIC_ORIGIN is set (and names a host, not an IP address): the RP ID is its host, and clientDataJSON.origin must equal it exactly. With passkeys off, every other /api/auth/passkeys route answers 404.

200.description: Whether the page should offer passkeys

post.summary: Start adding a passkey to the signed-in account
post.description: Returns PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON (WebAuthn Level 3 §5.4) for navigator.credentials.create(), after PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON(): the account's random 64-byte user handle (made on first use, never the row id), residentKey and userVerification required, attestation none, algorithms -8, -7 and -257, the account's existing passkeys in excludeCredentials, and credProps. Needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes (403 otherwise; ASVS V3.7.1). With {"mediation": "conditional"} it is an automatic passkey upgrade: only for a session under five minutes old, with userVerification "preferred", and the one registration whose response may lack the UP and UV flags. Sets the cookie binding the ceremony to this browser; replaces any registration the account had open. At most 50 passkeys per account.

200.description: Creation options; the ceremony cookie is set

403.description: No sign-in in the last 10 minutes (or, for an upgrade, the last five); sign in again and retry

503.description: Too many unfinished passkey ceremonies across the site

post.description: Takes the credential's JSON (credential.toJSON()). Verified per WebAuthn Level 3 §7.1: the challenge is found by its SHA-256 and used up before anything else (single use, five minutes, issued for a registration to this account and to this browser's ceremony cookie); clientDataJSON type webauthn.create, origin exactly PUBLIC_ORIGIN, not cross-origin; rpIdHash; UP and UV (except for an upgrade); BS only with BE; attested credential data present, credential ID at most 1023 bytes and equal to rawId; the key's algorithm one of those offered, RSA at least 2048 bits. fmt none must have an empty statement; any other format is accepted with its statement unread (no attestation trust). A client reporting credProps.rk false is refused. Malformed input — CBOR included — is a 400, never a 500.

201.description: Stored; the ceremony cookie is cleared

400.description: Unreadable, expired, used, issued for something else, or refused by a check

409.description: That credential ID is already registered (to any account), or the account has 50 passkeys

post.summary: Start creating an account with a passkey and no password
post.description: The same username rule and the same per-address throttle as POST /api/auth/signup, counted at the same point: a malformed name is free, a taken one counts as a probe, and everything that gets as far as issuing a challenge counts. No account is made here — only once the passkey verifies. The new account's user handle travels with the ceremony.

200.description: Creation options; the ceremony cookie is set

503.description: Too many unfinished passkey ceremonies across the site

post.summary: Finish creating an account with a passkey
post.description: Verified as for register/verify (UP and UV required). Then the account — with no password — and its passkey are created in one transaction, and a fresh session is started, as a password signup does.

201.description: Account created and signed in; the session cookie is set and the ceremony cookie cleared

400.description: Unreadable, expired, used, issued for something else, or refused by a check

409.description: The username was taken while the passkey was being made, or the credential ID is already registered

post.summary: Start signing in with a passkey
post.description: Returns PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON (§5.5) with an empty allowCredentials — any discoverable credential for this RP ID — and userVerification required. The sign-in page asks for these as it loads, for autofill (conditional mediation). A browser replacing a ceremony of its own (it sends the previous ceremony cookie) adds no row and isn't throttled; otherwise the request counts against the address, and is given back when that sign-in completes.

200.description: Request options; the ceremony cookie is set

503.description: Too many unfinished passkey ceremonies across the site

post.summary: Finish signing in with a passkey
post.description: Counted against the address before anything is read. Verified per §7.2: the challenge used up first (single use, five minutes, a sign-in challenge, this browser's); the credential found by id among those for this RP ID; userHandle present and equal to the owning account's handle; clientDataJSON type webauthn.get, origin exact, not cross-origin; rpIdHash; UP and UV; BE unchanged since registration; the signature over authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON). The signature counter must rise once either side is non-zero; a regression is refused and logged as a possible clone. A fresh session as for a password login. An unknown credential answers 401 with unknown_credential: true, for PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential().

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set and the ceremony cookie cleared

401.description: Expired, used, from another browser, unknown (unknown_credential: true), or refused by a check

get.description: With what the page's Signal API calls need (rp_id, user_handle) and how many ways in the account has (sign_in_methods), so the page can grey out removing the last one.

200.description: The account's passkeys, oldest first

patch.description: The name loses control characters and is cut to 60 characters; an empty one is refused. Another account's passkey answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

200.description: Renamed

delete.description: Refused with 409 when it is the last way to sign in (signInMethodCount(): a password, providers configured now, passkeys for the current RP ID). A passkey made for another RP ID never counted and can always be removed. Another account's passkey answers 404.

200.description: Removed

409.description: It is the only remaining way to sign in

post.summary: Change the password, or set a first one
post.description: With a password set, current_password is required (ASVS V2.1.6). An account made through a provider has none to give, so setting a first one needs a session that signed in within the last 10 minutes instead (ASVS V3.7.1); otherwise 403. The new password follows the signup rules (NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2: at least 8 characters, not a common password, not containing the username, not one character repeated) and must differ from the current one. Refusals that cost no hash are not counted; everything else is, per address and per account-within-address, before any hash — ten per 15 minutes. On success every other session of the account ends (ASVS V3.3.3) and this one gets a new token in Set-Cookie; the session keeps its id and sign-in time. If the session is ended while the password is being hashed, nothing is saved (401).

200.description: Changed; other sessions ended and this session's cookie replaced

401.description: Not signed in, the current password is wrong, or the session ended before the change was saved

409.description: The password was changed by another request while this one was being checked

503.description: Every password-hashing slot is busy; retry in a moment

get.summary: Every browser signed in to this account
get.description: ASVS V3.3.4. Sessions that are still usable, most recently used first. id is a random public handle; the token and its hash never leave the server. No IP addresses are stored or returned (GDPR data minimisation).

200.description: The account's live sessions

post.description: Ends every session of this account except the one making the request. Needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes (ASVS V3.3.4, "having re-entered login credentials"), so an old stolen cookie can't end its owner's sessions.

200.description: Ended

delete.summary: End one of this account's sessions
delete.description: Ending another browser's session needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes (403 otherwise). Ending the session making the request is signing out: always allowed, and the cookie is cleared. Another account's session — or an id that isn't 32 lowercase hex characters — answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

200.description: Ended. Set-Cookie clears the cookie when it was this session.

get.summary: The signed-in account, with how many trees it owns
get.description: What the account page shows before deletion: deleting the account deletes these trees too.

200.description: The account

delete.summary: Delete the account and every tree it made
delete.description: GDPR Art. 17 (erasure). In one transaction: every tree the account owns (with its skills and links), then the account, whose sessions, connected sign-ins and unfinished provider sign-ins go with it. confirm_username must equal the username, case-insensitively. password is required when the account has one; otherwise the session must have signed in within the last 10 minutes (403). A wrong username or missing password is not counted towards the limit; a wrong password is, before the hash. The response clears the cookie and sends Clear-Site-Data: "cookies", "storage".

200.description: Deleted; the session cookie and this site's browser storage are cleared

401.description: Not signed in, the password is wrong, or the session ended before the deletion

503.description: Every password-hashing slot is busy; retry in a moment

get.summary: Download everything held about the account
get.description: GDPR Art. 15 (access) and Art. 20 (portability): one JSON attachment, skilltrees-<username>.json, holding the account, its connected sign-ins, its sessions' metadata, its passkeys' names and dates (when passkeys exist on this server), and every tree it owns in the portable format of FORMAT.md — each of which can be sent to POST /api/trees/import as it is. Never included: the password hash, session tokens or their hashes, passkey key material. Ten exports per account per 15 minutes.

200.description: The export, as a download
Every tree, with its skill count

post.summary: Create a tree owned by the signed-in account

get.summary: One tree with its skills and prerequisite links

200.description: The tree, its skills and its links

patch.summary: Change a tree's title, description or author
patch.description: Only the account that owns the tree may do this. Trees created before accounts existed have no owner and are read-only for everyone.

200.description: The updated tree

delete.summary: Delete a tree and everything in it

200.description: Deleted

post.summary: Add a skill to a tree

200.description: The updated skill

delete.summary: Delete a skill and its links

200.description: Deleted

post.summary: Link one skill as a prerequisite of another
post.description: Both skills must belong to this tree, and the link must not create a cycle.

200.description: Deleted

get.summary: Download a tree in the portable format

parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: Override the tree's own layout mode.

200.description: The tree as a portable JSON document

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename derived from the tree title.

post.summary: Download a tree, supplying on-screen coordinates
post.description: Dragging a skill is session-only and never saved, so the browser sends its current arrangement with the request when exporting as manual.

200.description: The tree as a portable JSON document

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename derived from the tree title.

post.summary: Create a tree from a portable JSON document
Receive CSP violation reports from browsers
post.description: The endpoint pages name in Reporting-Endpoints (csp-endpoint) and in their CSP's report-to and report-uri. Takes the Reporting API's application/reports+json (an array of reports) and CSP2's application/csp-report (one report). Bodies are capped at 64 KB; the endpoint is throttled per address (10 per 15 minutes). Each report is logged as one line, with query strings removed from its URLs; nothing is stored.

SessionCookie.name: skilltree_session
SessionCookie.description: Opaque 256-bit session token. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/. Over HTTPS the cookie is named __Host-skilltree_session, is Secure, and is the only name accepted there; skilltree_session is used over plain http (localhost) only.

SetSessionCookie.description: Sets or clears the session cookie.

SetFlowCookie.description: Sets (on start) or clears (on callback) the cookie binding a provider sign-in to this browser: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, ten minutes; __Host-skilltree_oauth and Secure over HTTPS. The callback also sets the session cookie when it signs someone in.

SetPasskeyCookie.description: Sets (on options) or clears (on verify) the cookie binding a passkey ceremony to this browser: a fresh random value each time, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, five minutes; __Host-skilltree_webauthn and Secure over HTTPS. A verify that signs someone in sets the session cookie as well.

ClearSiteDataErase.description: W3C Clear Site Data, on account deletion: cookies and this site's browser storage (sessionStorage, localStorage, IndexedDB), but not the HTTP cache — nothing personal is cached — and not executionContexts.

ETag.description: Strong validator for this representation (RFC 9110 §8.8.3), distinct per Content-Encoding. Send it back in If-None-Match to get a 304 when nothing changed.

Accept.description: The request media types this operation takes (RFC 9110 §15.5.16).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again (RFC 9110 §10.2.3).

RateLimitPolicy.description: The quota policy that was hit, as an Internet-Draft structured field (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11): q is the quota, w the window in seconds. Advisory until the draft is published.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota (r) and seconds until it is restored (t), per the same draft.

SessionId.name: id
SessionId.description: A session's public id, from GET /api/auth/sessions. Random, and unrelated to the session token.

NotModified.description: The If-None-Match validator still matches; use the stored copy

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or failed validation

Unauthorized.description: Not signed in, or the credentials were wrong

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but this is not your tree (or it has no owner and is read-only); or a cross-site request (Fetch Metadata, or an Origin that isn't this host)

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but doesn't take this method. Not listed per operation, since it answers the methods that aren't there.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body wasn't declared as a type this operation takes (application/json unless stated), wasn't UTF-8, or was content-encoded

SignInAgain.description: This needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes (ASVS V3.7.1): setting a first password or deleting an account that has none, ending another browser's session, or adding a passkey. Sign out and in again, then retry.

ValidationProblems.description: The document was rejected, with a list of reasons

Error.description: An RFC 9457 problem details object. type is about:blank, so title is the HTTP status phrase; detail says what went wrong. error repeats detail for clients written before problem details.

ValidationError.description: A problem details object (see Error) that also lists each reason the document was rejected.

ReportList.description: A Reporting API upload (W3C Reporting API): a list of reports. Only type and body are read.

has_password.description: False for an account made through a provider or with a passkey, which has no password.

passkeys.description: How many passkeys can sign in to it here (made for the current RP ID); 0 when passkeys are off.

intent.description: login signs in (making an account for an identity never seen before, never matching by email). link connects the provider account to the signed-in account.

next.description: Where to go afterwards: a path on this site. Anything else — another origin, //host, /\host, a control character — falls back to /#browse (login) or /account.html (link).

authorization_url.description: The provider's authorization endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (built from PUBLIC_ORIGIN), scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256 and, for OpenID Connect, nonce.

display_name.description: Which account at the provider this is, for display only (a GitHub login, a preferred username or email).

enabled.description: Whether it can sign in now: its provider is configured, under the same issuer.

Base64Url.description: Unpadded base64url (RFC 4648 §5), as WebAuthn's JSON forms use for binary members. Must be canonical: exactly the encoding of the bytes it decodes to.

mediation.description: Ask for an automatic passkey upgrade (conditional create) rather than an ordinary registration.

id.description: The user handle: 64 random bytes, never the account's row id.

excludeCredentials.description: The account's passkeys for this RP ID; empty for a sign-up.

PasskeyRegistrationResponse.description: RegistrationResponseJSON (§5.1), as credential.toJSON() returns it. Members not listed are ignored.

PasskeyAuthenticationResponse.description: AuthenticationResponseJSON (§5.1), as credential.toJSON() returns it. Members not listed are ignored.

userHandle.description: Required: sign-in uses discoverable credentials, and this names the account.

name.description: The owner's label. New passkeys are named after a known provider's AAGUID ("iCloud Keychain"), or "Passkey".

credential_id.description: For the Signal API. Not a secret; only its owner is shown it.

backup_eligible.description: The BE flag: fixed when it was made.

backed_up.description: The BS flag as of the last sign-in: synced to other devices.

enabled.description: Made for the RP ID in force now, so it can sign in here — the rule signInMethodCount() counts by.

user_handle.description: The account's user handle, or null if it has never had a passkey.

sign_in_methods.description: Ways in the account has now: a password, providers configured now, passkeys usable here.

name.description: Control characters removed, trimmed and cut to 60 characters.

PasskeyError.description: Problem details, plus unknown_credential: true when the passkey presented isn't registered here — the page then calls PublicKeyCredential.signalUnknownCredential().

current_password.description: Required when the account has a password; ignored when it has none.

user_agent.description: As the browser sent it, cut to 256 characters, control characters removed; empty when unknown. Caller-supplied: a label, not proof.

current.description: Whether this is the session making the request.

confirm_username.description: The account's username, typed to confirm; compared case-insensitively.

password.description: Required when the account has a password.

AccountExport.description: Everything held about one account. Times are UTC, in the Timestamp format.

passkeys.description: Present only when this server stores passkeys.

ExportedIdentity.description: A connected sign-in. issuer and subject are what link it to this account; on their own they sign nobody in.

ExportedPasskey.description: A passkey's id, name, created_at and last_used_at, read by an allow-list of columns. Never key material, credential ids, AAGUIDs or counters.

LayoutMode.description: manual: stored coordinates are authoritative. auto: coordinates are ignored and the layout is computed from structure.

Timestamp.description: SQLite datetime('now') output in UTC: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Note this is not RFC 3339 (no 'T' separator, no offset).

featured.description: 1 for the homepage spotlight. Set server-side only; ignored if supplied in a request.

user_id.description: Owning account. null means the tree predates accounts and is read-only for everyone.

positions.description: Map of skill id to on-screen coordinates.

id.description: Slug, unique within the document. Skills reference each other by slug, never by database id.

requires.description: Slugs of the skills required before this one. All are required together.

Notation.description: The portable tree format described in FORMAT.md.
